summary: Follow-up to the 2026-06-02 production incident where Argosy observed increased 5xxs and latency spikes tied to KV cache evictions and an autoscaler edge case. We reviewed root cause, current mitigations, next steps for patching the memory leak in the model server, and agreed on a change window plus additional alerting and canary rollout plans. Redwood offered temporary dedicated capacity to stabilize traffic during the fix and will share postmortem artifacts and security docs.
topics: Root cause: KV cache eviction + autoscaler race + memory leak
Immediate mitigations applied (scaling policy, emergency restart)
Reliability improvements: alerting, canary rollouts, soak tests
Security/compliance ask: audit logs, KMS details
transcript: [00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we wanted to run through the postmortem follow up for the june second incident - i know this has been rough, so first, quick round of intros?
[00:12] Maya Johnson: Maya here — head of platform at Argosy. Thanks for organizing. we got hit pretty hard that afternoon, so—
[00:18] Ethan Cruz: Ethan, SRE. we captured a bunch of metrics and heap dumps, i'll share those post call, but we saw a sharp rise in 5xxs and token latency around 14:23 UTC
[00:28] Jules Ortega: Jules from Redwood, SE. thanks. quick note — transcription likely mangled some of the k v cache terms in the doc you saw, i can clarify as we go
[00:35] Priya Nair: Priya, CISO. I'll mainly be listening for the security/risk mitigations and retention of logs at this point
[00:44] Samir Patel: Great. quick agenda: 1) short incident recap, 2) root cause and evidence, 3) what we've patched so far, 4) mitigations & reliability roadmap, 5) next steps and change window

[01:00] Jules Ortega: Recap — at ~14:20 we saw a cascade: KV cache eviction rate spiked, which increased cold starts for model shards, combined with an autoscaler race that left pods under-provisioned briefly. that in turn exposed a memory leak in a particular model server binary which caused OOM restarts and 503s. network was fine, no region failover triggered
[01:28] Maya Johnson: the part i want to confirm — was it the LRU eviction or TTL based? our ops graph shows a bunch of tombstones and eviction churn

[01:36] Jules Ortega: looks like LRU churn due to an unexpected workload pattern; TTLs weren't the primary factor. the model was pinning large KV entries during some prompt patterns which pushed memory usage up

[02:05] Ethan Cruz: i can confirm we saw the k v miss rate jump; also a subtle thing — the autoscaler scale-down probes overlapped with a burst, so capacity dipped when it needed to be up. there was a 30s window where throughput dropped by ~40%

[02:35] Samir Patel: that's the autoscaler race we referenced in the postmortem doc. we pushed an emergency change to increase min replicas and bumped memory on the model pods as immediate mitigation — that removed the OOM restarts for the last 48 hours
[03:02] Priya Nair: what about audit/log retention? we need to keep full request logs for 90 days for this workload per our compliance policy

[03:12] Ava Lin: Ava from CS — Redwood can provide audit logs exports and we've scoped an S3 delivery for Argosy for 90-day retention. samir will include the recipe and required roles in the follow-up packet
[03:30] Maya Johnson: good. also we need to see the heap dump analysis. ethan, can you confirm you have those?
[03:38] Ethan Cruz: yes, i exported two heap dumps around the incident window; i'll attach to the support ticket. they're large so we'll use your secure upload link

[03:46] Jules Ortega: perfect — i'll correlate those with our runtime metrics. preliminary root cause is a rare codepath in the model server that leaks a KV reference when a certain quantized path is used. the runtime team already has a patch in review
[04:10] Maya Johnson: did the leak only affect customers using that quantized model variant?

[04:16] Jules Ortega: mostly, yes. customers on default model variants didn't hit it. argosy's production traffic pattern disproportionately exercised that codepath because of long-prefix prompts and frequent reranking requests

[04:40] Samir Patel: mitigation timeline: patch expected by 2026-06-11 from runtime team; we'll validate in staging, then run a canary on a small % of traffic, then full rollout. we recommended a change window week of 6/18
[05:02] Ethan Cruz: can we get temporary dedicated nodes or reserved capacity during the rollout? we'd prefer not to run at risky autoscaler settings while rolling the patch
[05:10] Samir Patel: yes — Redwood will provide temporary dedicated capacity credits for two weeks; that gives you a controlled floor for capacity while we patch
[05:20] Priya Nair: security questions: will the rollout require any secrets rotation or KMS changes?

[05:28] Jules Ortega: no KMS rotation required. the change is binary-level memory management fix. however, i'll attach the security review notes and the specific KMS/HSM configuration doc for your auditors
[05:48] Maya Johnson: alerting — currently our alerts only fired after the 5xx ramp. can we add a KV eviction rate alert and a cache miss anomaly detection?

[05:56] Jules Ortega: yep, recommended thresholds: KV eviction > 5% sustained for 3m, cache miss rate > 15% for 2m, and pod restart rate > 1 in 5m. we'll push alert rules to your account and provide terraform snippets
[06:18] Ethan Cruz: also want an end-to-end synthetic load test that replicates our 10k QPS peak with the long-prefix prompts — can redwood help run that?
[06:26] Samir Patel: we can — we'll schedule a joint benchmark with Redwood ops and your SREs. we'll need the exact prompt set and traffic mix; ethan please share that in the ticket
[06:40] Maya Johnson: what's the mitigation for the autoscaler race? can you tune the cool-downs?

[06:47] Jules Ortega: yes, two prongs: set a higher min-replicas for the route during high-variance windows, and adjust the scale-down cooldown to reduce flapping. we've also proposed an improved probe that errs on the side of keeping pods alive during bursts
[07:12] Priya Nair: any impact to our data residency or egress? auditors will ask if we moved logs or containers to other regions
[07:20] Ava Lin: no cross-region moves planned. temporary dedicated capacity will be in your same region and we'll provide region-specific audit logs. samir will include the network diagram

[07:36] Samir Patel: ok let's go over the doc list i'm going to send: 1) full postmortem PDF, 2) heap dump pointers & support ticket link, 3) security artifacts (SOC2 appendix, KMS config, network diagram), 4) terraform alert rules, 5) benchmark plan template
[07:56] Maya Johnson: that's good. please make the postmortem explicit about the timeline and the customer impact matrix — e.g., which routes had increased SLO breaches

[08:06] Jules Ortega: will do. on the topic of regressions — we'd like to add a quality/regression alert that ties to prompts/evals so if latency regresses after a change we can rollback automatically
[08:20] Ethan Cruz: automatic rollback sounds good, do you have runbooks for that?
[08:25] Samir Patel: yes we have a runbook for canary rollback and traffic split reversion, we'll share the runbook and also help set up the automation in the console
[08:40] Maya Johnson: can you summarize the top three reliability improvements we discussed?
[08:46] Jules Ortega: 1) KV/caching alerts + terraform rules, 2) autoscaler tuning + min-replicas + improved probes, 3) runtime patch + staged canary and soak tests
[09:02] Priya Nair: one more ask — we need proof that audit logs are tamper-evident. what's your mechanism?
[09:08] Ava Lin: we provide signed delivery to your S3 with an HMAC per-batch and we can integrate with your SIEM; details will be in the security packet

[09:22] Samir Patel: wrapping up, agreed next steps: samir sends docs by 6/11, jules opens ticket and tracks runtime patch, ethan uploads heap dumps and prompt set, ava coordinates change window for 6/18. any objections?
[09:38] Maya Johnson: none. appreciate you moving quickly on this
[09:42] Ethan Cruz: i'll get the artifacts into the ticket today
[09:45] Priya Nair: thanks all, we'll review the packet and revert with any audit questions
[09:50] Samir Patel: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the calendar invites for the change window and a benchmark slot. i'll mark action items in the ticket
[09:58] Jules Ortega: thanks — and note, the runtime patch is targeted to close the memory leak in the quantized codepath; if anything changes we'll escalate immediately
[10:09] Ava Lin: ok call end, thanks folks
[10:12] (call ends)
